$comment: Source fields a review resolved by reading a publisher's data, applied by `buildSourceRegister` over the rows it derives from the research CSV. An input to the build rather than an edit of its output, for the same reason as `license-decisions.json`: the build rewrites the register whole, so a field recorded in the output is erased by the next run with no error and a normal-looking count.
$whyNotTheCSV: The research CSV records `address_role`, `coverage` and `upstream` as the placeholders `varies`, `country-specific` and the empty string on all 389 of its non-rail rows, and has no column for a personal-data review. That CSV is the record of what one research pass found on 2026-09-18, so a later review records its own findings here rather than by rewriting the pass's record.
$shape: Each key is a `sourceID` the register declares. Each value carries any of `addressRoles`, `coverage`, `upstreamLineage` and `personalDataReview`, which replace the derived row's values. See `@mailwoman/corpus/source-register`'s `AddressSourceRecord`.
$addressRoles: Keyed by the address column's path in the published record, because a publication can carry two roles on one record. `ingestEligibilityProblems` requires at least one column to have a role.
$upstreamLineage: The endpoint or dataset this source's copy was taken from, so two register rows fed by one upstream submission count as one observation rather than two. A URL when the upstream is not itself a register row.
$sireneRepetition: Nine rows below are one source, INSEE's SIRENE establishment register, split by overseas territory. The fields repeat because the register carries one row per jurisdiction and each row's coverage statement is about that territory, while the column layout and the diffusion mechanism are SIRENE's and identical throughout.
$sireneSecondAddress: SIRENE's establishment file carries a second address family, the `2`-suffixed columns, which INSEE labels only `adresse secondaire` — `complementAdresse2Etablissement` reads `Complément d'adresse secondaire`. What role that address plays is unstated, so it takes no entry in `addressRoles` rather than a guessed one, and the coverage text names it so a reader knows the column exists.
$ocdsPartyRoles: An OCDS release keys its addresses by party role, so `addressRoles` names roles rather than columns for those sources. A role is assigned only where OCDS's own codelist defines it, retrieved from `https://standard.open-contracting.org/1.1/en/codelists/partyRole.csv`: `buyer`, `procuringEntity`, `payer`, `funder` and `reviewBody` are bodies acting in the process, so their address is an office they operate and reads `facility`; `supplier` and `tenderer` are the transacting party, so theirs reads `counterparty`. Germany's release also uses eight roles from an extension whose codelist neither the 1.1 nor the latest list defines — `processContactPoint`, `reviewContactPoint`, `submissionReceiptBody`, `mediationBody`, `evaluationBody`, `procurementServiceProvider`, `leadTenderer`, `subcontractor` — and those take no role here rather than a guessed one.

es-mixed-regulatory-1.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of the Dirección General del Catastro, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://www.catastro.hacienda.gob.es/INSPIRE/Addresses/ES.SDGC.AD.atom.xml`, 681,783 bytes, sha256 `4342d37b6d5527eb7b8bebadc97966c90f1a041068ae9398b90183f2176898b9`, carrying `<updated>2026-08-21T00:00:00Z</updated>`. The feed lists 55 entries, and this row covers 52 of them. The other three belong to the Provincial Councils of Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa and Navarra, which publish their own cadastres through the same feed and state their own terms, `CC BY 3.0 ES`, `CC-BY-SA` and `CC BY 4.0`. Adding them needs a row each, because a decision scoped to one publisher cannot reach another. Each of the 52 entries links a province feed listing one zipped GML per municipality. The measured instance is Ceuta, `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.zip`, 354,647 bytes, whose one member `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` is 11,861,975 bytes and holds 8,126 `AD:Address` features. A feature is a point at a building entrance carrying a house-number designator, and it references a thoroughfare name, a postal descriptor and an administrative unit by `xlink:href`. The row count for the other 51 offices was not measured.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` was counted over all 11,861,975 bytes, so this covers the file rather than its first features. It holds 48 distinct element names and none of them names a party: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element, and no personal name of any kind. The only names are 505 `AD:ThoroughfareName`, 5 `AD:PostalDescriptor` and 1 `AD:AdminUnitName`. The file declares the INSPIRE Addresses 3.0 schema at `urn:x-inspire:specification:gmlas:Addresses:3.0`, which has no party element for another municipality to populate, so the reading rests on the schema as well as on the one municipality read. This is what separates the row from the other 25 `verified-corpus` sources: each of those is a business register or a procurement portal where the address belongs to a party, and some of those parties are natural persons trading on their own account. The cadastre's AD theme records the place. The ownership data that Spanish cadastral records also hold travels through a separate protected channel and appears nowhere in this dataset.

va-finance-1.coverage: ASIF's list of supervised entities for the Holy See, read from `https://www.asif.va/en/list-of-supervised-entities`, which is the row's `sourceURL` since the 2026-09-30 rights review corrected it. The 2026-09-18 pass recorded `https://www.asif.va/ENG/EntiVigilati.aspx`; on 2026-09-30 that path redirected to `https://www.asif.va/en/enti-vigilati` and answered HTTP 404 with an empty body, while the corrected path answered HTTP 200. The whole page is 3,254 bytes and the list has one member, `Institute for the Works of Religion (IOR)`, named without an address. The only address on the page is ASIF's own footer, `Palazzo San Carlo, 00120 Città del Vaticano`, which belongs to the regulator rather than to a supervised entity. So the register row's note that the list `exposes the regulated entity and Vatican postal address` is not borne out, and this publication is not an address source. `addressRoles` stays unresolved because there is no address column to assign a role to.

personalDataReview.because: The list has one member and it is an institution, the Institute for the Works of Religion. The page gives no address for it and names no natural person, so a corpus built from this publication would hold no record about an identifiable person. The reading follows from the page being read in full at 3,254 bytes rather than from a sample.

sj-business-legal-1.coverage: Svalbard records in Brønnøysund's Enhetsregisteret, the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities, reached through its open-data API. Read from Brønnøysund's own API documentation rather than from a data sample: the record carries three named address families, `forretningsadresse` the business address, `postadresse` the postal address and `beliggenhetsadresse` the location address, each with `adresse`, `postnummer`, `poststed`, `kommune`, `land` and `landkode`. Three families with three roles on one record is the richest shape of the sources measured so far. The Svalbard subset's row count is unmeasured: the API serves the national register and no count was taken over its Svalbard rows.

personalDataReview.because: Enhetsregisteret registers `enkeltpersonforetak`, sole proprietorships, so a record can name a natural person and give three addresses for them. No measurement was taken over the Svalbard subset, so this reading rests on the register's composition rather than on a count, and the count is the work that would narrow it. The shape matches SIRENE's: a national business register whose sole traders are natural persons.

it-procurement-grants-1.coverage: ANAC's OCDS release, Jan 2020 through Sep 2025 per the OCP Data Registry, 1,474,656 parties and 0 documents. Measured over the whole 2025 file, 3,963,957 bytes: 9,405 contracting processes and 29,823 party objects in three roles — supplier 11,075, buyer 9,381, payer 9,367. A buyer carries locality, postalCode, countryName and streetAddress on 9,381 of 9,381 rows. A payer carries a postcode on 9,355, a locality on 9,292 and a street line on 2,555. **The supplier role carries no address field at all**, so every address in this release belongs to a public body rather than to a contracting counterparty. Postcodes include the literal placeholder `N.A.`, which a reader has to treat as absent rather than as a code.

personalDataReview.because: The publication names identifiable natural persons and records an address for none of them, which is what this reading turns on. Two of 11,075 supplier party names take the `Surname, Firstname` form, so `absent` would be wrong. **The supplier role carries no `address` object at all**: 0 of 11,075 supplier parties hold one, re-measured on 2026-09-30 over the whole 2025 file, 9,405 contracting processes and 29,823 party objects. Every address in the release sits on `buyer`, 9,381 of 9,381, or on `payer`, 9,359 of 9,367, and both roles are held by Italian public entities. This source's `addressRoles` names those two fields alone, so an adapter built from the register reads no supplier field. A false-positive check on the reading: 35 party objects carry both an address and an inverted `Surname, Firstname` name, and reading all 35 finds public bodies whose name holds a comma, such as `SETTORE PATRIMONIO, AMBIENTE E LAVORI PUBBLICI` and `PARCO NAZIONALE DEL CILENTO, VALLO DI DIANO E ALBURNI`. The policy this reading applies is that a corpus carries no address of an identifiable natural person and does carry the addresses of organizations.

zm-procurement-grants-1.coverage: ZPPA's OCDS release, Aug 2016 through May 2026 per the OCP Data Registry, 483,215 parties and 115,495 documents. Measured over the whole 2026 file, 13,244,085 bytes: 26,157 contracting processes and 62,736 party objects in four roles — tenderer 36,146, buyer 26,590, procuringEntity 26,590, supplier 5,014. A tenderer carries region, locality, countryName and streetAddress on 36,146 of 36,146 rows and a postcode on 29,982. Buyer and procuringEntity carry the same four on 26,590 of 26,590, and a sample shows one party holding both roles. A supplier carries region, locality and countryName on 5,014. The street field sometimes holds a post-office box — the Civil Aviation Authority reads `P.O.Box 50137` in `streetAddress` — so the field's grammar is mixed and a premise parser trained on it would see mailing forms.

personalDataReview.because: Two measures were run and neither establishes `absent`. No supplier or tenderer name among 36,146 counterparty party objects takes the `Surname, Firstname` form. Every one of those 36,146 carries an organization identifier under scheme `ZM-PCR`, and that settles nothing about the party's kind: PACRA registers sole-proprietor business names alongside companies, so both kinds of party carry the number. Of 9,500 distinct counterparty names, 853 carry no legal-form marker, and a sole trader trading under a shop name reads as a business by every shape test — `KAVULAMUNGU BARGAIN CENTRE` and `NDANJI SHOPPING CENTRE` among them. Every counterparty role here carries a street address on 100% of rows, so the exposure is whatever share of those 9,500 are individuals, which no measure available here bounds.

cl-procurement-grants-1.coverage: ChileCompra's OCDS release, Jan 2022 through May 2026 per the OCP Data Registry, 11,619,010 parties and 4,864,820 documents — the largest of the ten procurement publications. personalDataReview.because: Two measures were run and neither establishes `absent`. personalDataReview.because: SIRENE registers `entrepreneurs individuels`, so a row can name a natural person and give an address for them. INSEE records an objection per row and places the obligation on the reuser: `il est ainsi de votre responsabilité de tenir compte du statut de diffusion le plus récent de chaque personne physique`. A row whose `statutDiffusionEtablissement` reads `P` is diffused partially after an objection, and for a natural person `l'identité de l'entrepreneur (nom, prénoms…), l'adresse dans la commune et la géolocalisation seront masquées`. That status changes after a corpus is built, so a frozen corpus and a model trained on it keep an address INSEE has since stopped diffusing. Filtering on the status is mechanical; discharging a continuing obligation from a published artifact is the open question.

au-procurement-grants-1.coverage: OCDS releases for Apr 2007 through Sep 2026, retrieved monthly by the OCP Data Registry, last on 2026-09-13. Measured on the 2022 release: 51,829 contracting processes, each carrying one supplier party and one procuring-entity party.
